security_audit.summary: All 23 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, fixed date substitutions, JMESPath backticks, or links to official AWS documentation. The skill still presents a medium-risk operational concern because its workflow recommends destructive AWS actions that require explicit approval and environment-specific validation.

remediation.issue: The workflow recommends deleting or terminating AWS resources and offers to generate deletion scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Default to read-only analysis, require explicit approval for each mutation, show exact resource identifiers, and use dry-run or backup controls where available.

content.user_title: Optimize AWS Spending and Reduce Cloud Waste
content.value_statement: AWS spending can grow without clear ownership or evidence. This skill uses Cost Explorer, resource inventory, and CloudWatch data to prioritize savings actions.
actual_capabilities: Breaks AWS costs down by service, region, and resource tags.
Compares spending periods to identify trends and increases.
Finds unattached EBS volumes, unused Elastic IPs, old snapshots, and low-utilization compute resources.
Uses CloudWatch metrics to support EC2 and RDS rightsizing recommendations.
Produces prioritized savings plans, checklists, and leadership reports.
limitations: Requires configured AWS CLI credentials and sufficient read permissions.
Example date commands use GNU date syntax and may not work unchanged on macOS.
Recommendations require workload context before deletion, termination, rightsizing, or commitment purchases.
Savings estimates depend on current pricing, usage history, tags, and available metrics.

use_cases.title: Review Monthly Cloud Spend
use_cases.description: Compare recent AWS costs by service and identify the largest spending increases.

use_cases.title: Find Idle Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Inventory unused storage, addresses, snapshots, and low-utilization compute before a cleanup review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Savings Roadmap
use_cases.description: Turn usage evidence into prioritized actions, estimated savings, and a leadership summary.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize AWS Costs
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze read-only AWS costs for the last three months. Break down spending by service and highlight the five largest month-over-month changes.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory Idle Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Find unattached EBS volumes, unused Elastic IPs, and snapshots older than 90 days. Return resource identifiers, regions, age, and estimated monthly savings.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Compute Rightsizing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review 30 days of EC2 and RDS utilization. Recommend rightsizing candidates with evidence, expected savings, performance risks, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Optimization Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 90-day AWS cost optimization roadmap. Rank actions by savings, effort, and risk. Require approval before any resource change.

output_examples.input: Compare this month with last month and identify the main cost drivers.
output: EC2 increased by 18 percent and contributed the largest absolute change.
Data transfer increased by 11 percent, concentrated in one region.
Validate deployment growth and cross-region traffic before changing resources.

output_examples.input: Find quick savings opportunities without changing resources.
output: Seven unattached EBS volumes are candidates for owner review.
Three Elastic IPs have no current association.
Keep the assessment read-only until owners approve each action.

output_examples.input: Prepare a rightsizing summary for leadership.
output_examples.output: The review identifies prioritized EC2 and RDS candidates, estimated savings, supporting utilization metrics, operational risks, and approval steps.

best_practices: Start with read-only permissions and preserve the evidence used for each recommendation.
Confirm ownership, backups, dependencies, and rollback plans before changing any resource.
Validate savings estimates against current pricing and review results after implementation.
anti_patterns: Do not delete, stop, or resize resources based only on low utilization.
Do not purchase commitments without stable usage history and coverage analysis.
Do not expose account identifiers, resource names, or cost reports beyond authorized recipients.

faq.question: What AWS access does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs configured AWS CLI credentials and read access to Cost Explorer, resource inventories, and relevant CloudWatch metrics.

faq.question: Does the skill change AWS resources automatically?
faq.answer: The documented analysis commands are read-only. Any generated mutation command requires separate review, explicit approval, and suitable AWS permissions.

faq.question: Can it estimate potential savings?
faq.answer: Yes. Estimates depend on current pricing, usage history, resource metadata, and the completeness of available metrics.

faq.question: Which resources can it review?
faq.answer: It covers EC2, EBS, Elastic IPs, snapshots, RDS, S3 lifecycle opportunities, Lambda memory, logs, and commitment options.

faq.question: Will every example command work on macOS?
faq.answer: No. Several examples use GNU date options, so macOS users may need compatible date syntax or GNU core utilities.

faq.question: How should recommendations be validated?
faq.answer: Review workload dependencies, ownership, backups, performance requirements, pricing, and rollback plans before implementing any recommendation.
